title: C13 consolidation recipe v0 (registry artifact — WHAT WE TRAIN)
description: One versioned training recipe, served verbatim by storage's registry at GET /recipes/{recipe_id}. `recipe_id` == the filename stem, and the registry refuses to serve a file whose own `recipe_id` disagrees with the id it was asked for — a registry that silently returned a differently-identified artifact would let a night mis-record what it trained under. GLOBAL AND VERSIONED, NEVER PER-USER: `recipe_id` is hashed into continuum's amplify and train stage keys, so a per-user value would fork the id per user and destroy artifact comparability (this is also why a per-user boundary_local_time cannot ride C13 and belongs on C12 instead). THE GATE POLICY IS A SEPARATE ARTIFACT with its own id and its own schema (c13_gate_policy.v0.json), ratified with gate v1.1 on 2026-07-24: only the training recipe may enter a cycle stage key, so changing a publish threshold must never fork `recipe_id` or invalidate hours of GPU cache. ADDITIONAL PROPERTIES ARE DELIBERATELY ALLOWED (unlike every other contract here): these artifacts carry human provenance prose — `source`, `note`, and per-threshold rationale — and a registry that rejected a recipe for documenting itself would push that documentation out of the artifact and into a wiki. A mistyped knob is still caught, because the knobs that matter are `required`.

recipe_id.description: The recipe's identity AND its filename stem (`<recipes_dir>/<recipe_id>.json`). Path-safe by pattern because it resolves to a file: no slashes, no leading dot, no '..'. Every knob change forks it — the same posture as data-processing's `pipeline_version`; an artifact trained under recipe A is never silently comparable to one trained under recipe B.

source.description: Optional provenance prose: where these numbers came from and what was confirmed against what.

note.description: Optional prose: what changed relative to the recipe this one forked from, and whether artifacts stay comparable.

amplify.description: The amplification pass: how many retellings of each block, and how many of them are deny-then-correct negatives.

variants.description: Retellings per block (48 in the parity-locked v1.0).

neg_frac.description: Fraction of variants that are deny-then-correct negatives (0.15 in v1.0). Traps erode by ~night 12 without this pressure.

ok_rate_min.description: Minimum acceptable amplifier OK rate before the stage is treated as failed.

replay.description: The rehearsal mix — what rescues sequential consolidation from collapse. Generative replay demonstrably fails, so real past text is required forever.

frac.description: Replay budget as a fraction of the night's target chars (0.30 in v1.0). 0.0 is the SEQ arm — the reference's own negative control.

source.description: Which pool replay samples from: `amp` = the amplified corpora in the C14 reservoir (v1.0, the parity path); `rawlog` = prior day-logs re-read via C10 (the locked architecture; a measured tie, and simpler). A CLOSED enum because continuum raises on anything else — an unknown source must fail at fetch, not at 2am.

neg_boost.description: Re-exposure boost for deny-then-correct paragraphs during replay. 0.0 until the ported sampler lands; paragraphs are already tagged at admission for it.

train.description: The LoRA training pass. Parity-critical and frozen: these are the numbers the research line locked.

chunk_tokens.description: Token length the corpus is chunked to for continued pre-training.

objective.description: THE CORE INVARIANT OF THE WHOLE RESEARCH LINE, pinned as a single-value enum on purpose. Continued pre-training on the day's text — never supervised QA fine-tuning, which teaches the shape of an answer rather than the day. Widening this enum is a deliberate act that must be argued for, which is exactly why it is not a free-form string.

corpus.description: The DAY-LOG FORMAT knobs. These are the ones storage reads: they decide segment bucket width and block length, i.e. what a day-log looks like — which is why C10 bodies carry `recipe_id` beside `daylog_format_version`.

quality_min.description: Minimum segment quality admitted to training. The gate lives in continuum, not in the day log: low-quality rows are excluded from TRAINING, never from the record.

block_segments.description: Maximum segments per scene block (12 in v1.0 => ~2 min blocks at 10 s segments).

segment_seconds.description: Segment bucket width in seconds (10 in v1.0). Buckets sit on a GLOBAL epoch grid — floor(t_start / segment_seconds) — so a bucket does not depend on which window collected the record.

window.description: When the nightly cycle fires. NOT the window's extent — that is `[last_trained_t, now-delta)` on storage's ingest clock (D18) and needs no recipe and no timezone.

boundary_local_time.description: HH:MM in the user's C12 `home_tz` — the local hour the cycle fires. GLOBAL today, which is precisely what cannot express a night-shift worker; the per-user override is named as C12's expected second field and is deliberately not minted until it has a consumer.
